instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees and point them out to the sides in a W shape, palms facing forward.
3. Brace your core and press the dumbbells overhead in an arc until your arms are extended.
4. Bring the dumbbells slightly inward at the top so they finish over the middle of your body.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to the W position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and ribs down to protect your lower back.
2. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.
4. Use a lighter weight and controlled tempo.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell vertically with both hands cupped under the top weight plate.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body.
3. Curl the dumbbell upward toward your chin by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move the weight with your biceps and avoid swinging.
2. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
4. Keep your wrists firm to hold the dumbbell steady.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward and arms extended at your sides.
2. Keep your upper arms still and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
3. At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly in this palms-down position.
5. Rotate your wrists back to palms-up at the bottom.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower the weight slowly to load the forearms on the way down.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body.
3. Make the wrist rotation smooth and controlled.
4. Use a lighter weight than a standard curl.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and upper arms resting on the pad.
2. Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
3. At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly in this palms-down position.
5. Rotate your wrists back to palms-up at the bottom.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pressed against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Lower the weight slowly to overload the forearms.
3. Use a full range of motion.
4. Make the wrist rotation smooth and controlled.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your body.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, letting your arms hang down.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, keeping your elbows close and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Hold the contraction briefly.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your spine.
2. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
3. Lead with your elbows and drive with your back, not your arms.
4. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
